newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates rise on mill demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates rise on mill demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates rose on Saturday on demand from mill owners amid reports that the crop would be smaller than earlier estimated, dealers said.

"The crop position in the Punjab province is still not clear. But there are reports that the overall size of the crop will be well below the government's target of 10 million (375-lb) bales," dealer Kishan Chand said. "Now people expect the crop to be around 8.5 million bales to 9.0 million bales."
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 was traded at around 2,275 rupees ($56.56) to 2,300 per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
